title: SOLID cohesion coupling DRY KISS YAGNI
concepts: Design principles are decision aids that protect changeability and correctness; they are not laws that justify extra abstractions without a real need.
Cohesion describes how strongly a module's responsibilities belong together; coupling describes how much one module knows about or depends on another.
Good boundaries aim for strong cohesion inside and low, explicit coupling across modules, while recognizing that some dependencies are necessary.
SOLID principles address object-oriented responsibility, extension, substitutability, client-specific interfaces, and dependency direction.
DRY concerns duplicated knowledge that must change together, not every repeated line; KISS favors the simplest design that meets real requirements; YAGNI delays speculative capabilities.
Principles can conflict locally, so evaluate them against change frequency, correctness constraints, team comprehension, and the cost of indirection.
